elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 7.2 now reads "Customer is not required to disclose or match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives." The operative obligation ("Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer") is gone, and no other cited language imposes a most-favoured-customer/nation duty on Customer; Section 12.3 affirmatively recites that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment.

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit there is no Customer-side MFN at all (Section 7.2 expressly negates any disclose-and-match duty), so the product-scoping limitation is vacuously satisfied by the stronger preferred outcome.

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no Customer MFN survives in Section 7.2, so no duration cap is needed; the obligation has zero term rather than a limited one.

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with the disclose-and-match obligation eliminated there is no comparison mechanic requiring like-for-like carve-outs.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single element is met in operative text, not merely promised in the margin comment — Section 7.2 as rendered affirmatively negates any Customer duty to disclose or match third-party offers.
Fallback elements are vacuously met because no Customer-side MFN remains; the preferred position subsumes them.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to the one sentence creating the burden, converts it into a short negating statement without adding survival tails, procedures, damages categories, notice mechanics, or any Vendor-side obligation, and does not disturb the favourable Section 12.3 recital (left verbatim). Retaining a short negating sentence rather than a bare deletion is a concise way to reach the preferred level and does not duplicate Section 12.3's operative effect in a conflicting way.

Intent is preserved: no defined term is orphaned, no cross-reference dangles, the Section 7.2 numbering is retained so downstream references remain valid, and the previously contradictory Section 12.3 recital ("Customer has made no ... most-favoured-customer ... commitment") is now internally consistent with Section 7.2.
No Vendor-granted MFN in Customer's favour existed in the cited text, so nothing beneficial to us was removed, consistent with the redline guidance to keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

Deviation classification is supported: the original clause was an open-ended obligation to match any more favourable third-party offer with no product scope, no term, and no like-for-like carve-outs, failing all three fallback elements and touching walk-away territory.
